analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: Yesterday's NDX sell-off reflected fragile sentiment around AI financing. No single catalyst explains it. News chatter about a possible US/Israeli strike after the midterms may have set off a broader tech-led de-risking.

The JPM cash desk saw elevated de-grossing. Long-only accounts were 3x better for sale and hedge funds were 2.6x better to buy, mostly short covering. High-touch volumes ran +120% versus the 5-day moving average, and the overall desk was skewed 1.42x better sale.

Tech was the epicenter of flow. Selling was a mix of long and short, with very little demand to get long. The only real buying was in security software, and demand was very low in hyperscalers and neoclouds. Client sentiment is summarized as low positioning, low confidence, and nobody wanting to lean in first.

The cash desk's main concern is that the first inning of tech earnings, even good prints, is being met with waves of supply because investors are skittish on financing. Earnings expectations were remarkably high, and positioning is still not fully clean.

Pre-market, futures are mixed (SPX -0.2%, NDX flat, RTY -0.4%). NVDA is +0.7% and most of the Mag 7 are lower except TSLA +0.8%. OpenAI's $30bn funding round at a $1.25tn pre-money valuation came in below the previously reported $1.4tn target.

Rates: Treasury yields fell 15-21bp, the largest one-day decline since March 2023. The move began overnight amid risk aversion in European government bonds (EGBs), with French spread widening the focus. Yields have become increasingly correlated with the NASDAQ and negatively correlated with Brent.
The 10Y is still near 5% (4.970%), and the market-implied probability of a December hike fell to 88%. WTI is above $100 and Brent is near $114.

Euro area flash composite PMI fell 1.2pts to 51.9, a larger drop than JPM and consensus expected. It fully offsets the September gain and implies activity at a 1.4% annualized pace, near JPM's 1.5% 4Q26 GDP forecast. Output price pressures faded a little.

Feroli expects the October US flash manufacturing PMI at 54.5 versus 55.9 in September (best since summer 2022) and the flash services PMI at 58.0 versus 58.8. Both would be modest pullbacks from cycle highs and still in expansion.

September manufacturing PMI detail: output rose to 56.2 from 53.1, new orders to 56.1 from 54.3, and input prices ticked up to 65.6 from 65.2. Part of the new-orders gain came from front-loading ahead of higher prices and supply problems, plus AI-related investment demand. Output prices eased to 59.0 from 59.4.

September services PMI detail: new business hit a multi-year high of 58.5 and employment rose to 55.2 from a May trough of 47.3. Input prices jumped from 58.9 to 65.9, the fastest since late 2022, and output prices rose from 55.8 to 58.2, attributed to fuel, transportation and labor costs.

JPM credit desk (Jarvis): CCCs are down 4.22% YTD versus +0.09% for the HY index and are a major driver of HY underperformance. The CCC/B differential is 764bp, about 5bp from 12-month wides. CCCs are only 8.5% of the index and the performance attribution is heavily concentrated.

Credit desk trade idea: be in CCC and B risk during rate-hiking cycles. When rates spike over 3 months, BBs, Bs and CCCs averaged returns of -0.6%, +0.9% and +2.3%. Express via Portfolio Bond Basket TRS and/or HYCDX Junior Mezz and Equity tranches. Wait for signs of local stabilization, which the desk expects soon.

Market Intel view stays tactically bullish. Last week's sell-off was driven by two of the five flagged risks (Momentum / Tech Unwind and AI Credit Fears) while fundamentals held up. ASML and TSMC earnings were healthy and consumer data was resilient.

JPM does not expect the rotation out of tech to end abruptly, though its pace could moderate. It favors cyclical exposure outside tech while selectively buying tech weakness, particularly semis and memory, possibly through defined-risk options. Large-cap banks are of interest after a sharp pullback, via XLF.

Key catalysts: the inflation component of this week's PMIs, the Oct 28 Fed meeting (a hold would remove residual near-term hike risk, with focus on FY27 policy path remarks), sustained moderation in rates vol, and META earnings plus NVDA GTC Berlin as tests of AI revenue delivery.

Updated Monetization Menu (Oct 19): selective approach, preference for tech and a rebound via pairs trades and derivatives, constructive on Financials and Retailers, favor Brazil and Japan internationally, and monitoring Reopening opportunities that benefit from lower energy prices.
Near-term event calendar: Brazil runoff Oct 25, Israel election Oct 27, trade truce expiry Nov 1, US midterms Nov 3, US funding deadline Dec 11. Mag7 earnings (MSFT / GOOGL / AMZN) are due next week.

vol_and_positioning: Cash desk: long-only accounts 3x better for sale, hedge funds 2.6x better to buy (mostly covering). The overall desk was skewed 1.42x better sale, with high-touch volumes +120% versus the 5-day average.
Tech positioning is low and confidence is low. Demand for hyperscalers and neoclouds is very low, while security software saw the only real buying.
Rate hike-cycle credit positioning: CCC/B differential of 764bp sits near 12-month wides, and 1Q/4Q mutual fund performance dispersion is the tightest since 2005.
Credit desk notes that equity vol remains elevated with earnings in full swing and election season ahead, while new issue calendars have slowed and dealer inventory has normalized.
Risk list includes a spike in bond vol / equity vol. JPM wants sustained moderation in rates vol to support the broader rotation.
geopolitical: Chatter from several news articles about a possible US/Israeli strike after the midterms contributed to the tech-led de-risking.
A US/Iran deal is described as the biggest potential catalyst, which would squeeze EU and RTY higher.
The one-year trade truce between Trump and Xi expires Nov 1. NBC reports the US and China agreed to extend the truce through January 20, 2027.
French fiscal and political dynamics and possible ECB signaling on intervention are cited as needed to break the EGB widening cycle.
Elections: Brazil runoff Oct 25, Israel legislative election Oct 27, US midterms Nov 3.
Brent near $114 and WTI above $100 keep elevated energy prices as a market driver. The Ceasefire basket was among the worst performers in Europe.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings and macro support are intact. ASML and TSMC delivered healthy results, consumer data is resilient, and the AI sell-off has not come with deteriorating reported earnings. Lower yields already delivered part of the anticipated catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment around AI financing is fragile. Positioning and confidence are low, tech earnings are being met with supply, and the cash desk saw heavy de-grossing with little demand to get long.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed yield spike, a tech earnings miss (META results and NVDA GTC Berlin are the next tests), or a failure of rates vol to moderate.

tension_points.bull_case: CCCs are only 8.5% of the index, performance is concentrated, and CCCs and Bs have historically outperformed in rate-hiking cycles.
tension_points.bear_case: CCCs are down 4.22% YTD, the CCC/B differential of 764bp is near 12-month wides, and vol remains elevated with earnings and elections ahead.
